title: #IUIC | ##Deuteronomy28Project | Deuteronomy 28:36 | Southern Kingdom Edition #bible #sundayservice
segments: This is the book of Deuteronomy chapter
28 and verse 36. The Lord shall bring
thee and thy king which thou shalt set
over thee unto a nation which neither
thou nor thy fathers have known. And
there shalt thou serve other gods,
wooden stone.
During the transatlantic slave trade,
many African kings were brought over to
the western hemisphere to serve slavery.
Many native caciques were also sold into
slavery as well. Both represent the
southern kingdom and the northern
kingdom of Israel. Before finding
himself as a slave working hours on end
and living in hard conditions on the
frontier plantation in Jamaica, Tacky
was a Fante king from the Gold Coast,
now modern-day Ghana. In 1759, after
years of toiling and suffering on the
plantations, Tacky and his allies, Yaw,
Sobadu, and Quao Ten, who were also of
Ghanaian descent, escaped into a cave
far beyond their plantations to plan a
rebellion. They escaped during the day
when everyone was occupied with work or
at night and returning before daybreak.
With full support from Queen Nanny, who
was also of Ghanaian descent, Tacky's
plan was to defeat the British and all
slave masters and create a Jamaica as a
separate and independent black colony.
Unfortunately, he failed. He was
captured and hung and burnt alive.
